original.target_description: Study 8, at home: enjoyment of nonsocial external activities versus entertaining oneself with one’s thoughts; independent randomized conditions. Study number and enjoyment outcome establish correspondence, independently of row order or statistic values.

n.sample_role: Participants in the two mutually exclusive Study 8 enjoyment-comparison groups; analytic N summed from reported group counts.
n.exclusions: Not documented in supplied main article. Table 1 reports 15 participants in each Study 8 condition.
n.location: Table 1, Study 8: At home column headings; Study 8 paragraph beginning Would participants enjoy themselves more
n.quote: Study 8: At home ... Standard thought instructions ( n = 15) External activities ( n = 15) ... In study 8, we randomly assigned participants to entertain themselves with their own thoughts or to engage in external activities (such as reading a book, listening to music, or surfing the Web).

es.location: Study 8 paragraph, enjoyment comparison immediately following Table 1
es.quote: participants enjoyed the external activities much more than just thinking [ t (28) = 4.83, P < 0.001]

notes: Identity independently checked in supplied canonical text: title Just think: The challenges of the disengaged mind; all eight supplied authors; Science 2014 Jul 4;345(6192):75–77; DOI 10.1126/science.1250830. PMC author manuscript containing the main article, Table 1 and references; supplementary material is linked but its contents are not included. No PDF supplied. 15 standard-thought participants + 15 external-activity participants = 30 analytic participants. Table 1 identifies the two Study 8 groups; the Study 8 paragraph explicitly establishes random assignment to these mutually exclusive conditions and the enjoyment comparison. No N inferred from df. Exclusions not documented in supplied main article; these are the reported analysis-group counts, not recruitment counts. Only assigned unfinished fields populated. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. The supplied description summarizes the broader thinking-period procedure, but study_o explicitly identifies Study 8 and the named enjoyment outcome is reported for its external-activity versus thinking comparison. The supplied main article prints t (28) = 4.83, P < 0.001 for this test, not Cohen’s d; retain printed t without conversion. Same-test p bound is P < 0.001; p is unassigned and is not populated. Concentration and mind-wandering tests are different outcomes and are not selected.
